Management Plan
2026
OFFICE FOR ADMINISTRATION AND PAYMENT
OF INDIVIDUAL ENTITLEMENTS
1

PART 1. Introduction
Strategic planning and programming is the cornerstone of the Commission’s performance
management framework. The Commission’s strategic plan for 2025-2029 translates the
political priorities set in the Political Guidelines of President von der Leyen into general
objectives. This process ensures institutional coherence, enhances accountability, and aligns the
actions of all Commission services with the strategic vision of the mandate.
Within this framework, each Commission service has developed a strategic outlook for
2025-2029 in the Management plan 2025. This outlook defines a set of multiannual
objectives and indicators to measure progress towards their achievement. These will be used
for planning and reporting on performance throughout the period.
The 2026 management plan sets out what PMO intends to deliver this year to contribute to
these multiannual objectives (part 2). It also describes how PMO will contribute to the common
objective of building a modern and sustainable public administration (part 3). The main outputs
with their indicators and targets are presented in Annexes 1 and 2.
One of the key performance indicators of PMO is the indicator ‘Estimated risk at payment’
which is the Authorising Officer by Delegation's best conservative estimate of the amount of
relevant expenditure during the year, not in conformity with the contractual and regulatory
provisions applicable at the time the payment was made. The expenditure will subsequently be
subject to ex-post controls, and a proportion of the underlying errors will be detected and
corrected in subsequent years, corresponding to the conservatively estimated future
corrections. The difference between ‘Estimated risk at payment’ and estimated future
corrections results in the ‘Estimated risk at closure’, which for PMO remains usually the same
as ‘Risk at payment’. This is due to the fact that the PMO processes a very high number of
small transactions, which implies that the impact of corrections made after ex post controls
remains limited in comparison the overall amount of payments made.
The chart below illustrates the performance framework for PMO.
3

PART 2. Delivering on the Commission’s
priorities in 2026
The PMO contributes to the Commission’s general objective towards a modern, high
performing European public administration by:
• ensuring at all times the correct and timely handling of all types of transactions
• offering a high-quality customer service.
The achievement of these objectives is measured through the 6 Key Performance Indicators set
out in the Management Plan 2025. In addition, Part 2 reflects the priority actions and the most
important outputs PMO plans to deliver in 2026 and how these key outputs will contribute to
reaching these objectives.
1. Correct and timely handling of all types of
transactions
The PMO ensures the correct and timely handling of payments of salaries, pensions and
related entitlements as well as of unemployment benefits. The PMO strives to optimise
efficiency in operating the reimbursement of claims for medical expenses, missions, public
transport in Brussels as well as expenses incurred by experts and candidates. New intuitive
dashboards will allow for an improved monitoring and reporting.
The PMO significantly reduces the risk of errors associated with manual processing by using
new technologies and automation tools. The PMO Business Intelligence team continues to work
on mapping and analysing all workflows related to entitlements, to identify delays and
bottlenecks at each step. This analysis will be extended to other areas, resulting in a set of new
performance indicators as a powerful management tool to measure efficiency and identify
areas for improvement.
PMO also contributes to the setup of the Onboarding project (part of the HR
Transformation initiative), allowing the uploading and processing of documents needed for
pre-entry into service in a single platform, thus implementing the once-only approach. This
project is expected to result in efficiency gains and increased user satisfaction. Depending on
the finalisation of this project and on the budgetary availabilities, an equivalent project is
envisaged by DG HR for the Offboarding of staff, to which the PMO will be fully associated.
From a general perspective, PMO’s IT systems and applications ensure business continuity and
adequate support to guarantee quality of service and meet business needs. Several IT
developments are planned for 2026. The details of the achievements and ongoing major
activities are illustrated in Section 3.B of the present document.
2. High quality standards of customer service
The capacity of the PMO to provide quick answers to its customers' questions and requests sent
via the Staff Centre remains fundamental to the overall quality of its services. The client
5

satisfaction remains high – over 80% – and the aim for 2026 is to maintain this level of
positive feedback. The PMO strives to continuously improve client service, by analysing
available data and identifying possible areas of development.
The PMO communicates regularly through different channels: articles in Commission en Direct,
information via the announcements on MyIntracomm, articles in HR Staff Matters newsletters,
e-mail newsletters sent either to all staff, pensioners or targeted audiences. Furthermore, PMO
is in regular contact with the pensioners’ associations AIACE and SEPS (1). The PMO will
continue to inform its clients, be it Commission staff, staff of EUIBAs who have an SLA with
PMO, pensioners, beneficiaries of survival pensions or beneficiaries of the EU unemployment
allowance, about important updates and developments in 2026. At the same time, following
the launch of the Staff Centre, of the Pensioners’ Portal and of the Portal for former staff
members in 2025, in phase II of the project PMO will continue to address the clients’ feedback
to ensure correct and useful information for its fields of activity.
In 2026, the PMO will continue to offer online training and information sessions on financial
entitlements and health insurance for newcomers, as well as on missions and MiPS+ for
Commission services and new agencies adopting MiPS. In addition, monthly online training
sessions will be offered on end of service, transfer of pension rights and on the Pension
Scheme of the European Union; annual trainings will cover education allowance, while video
information capsules will showcase the practical steps to follow for the reimbursement of
medical expenses. PMO has already created several training capsules on pension topics that are
integrated in the new HR Offboarding portal, and this offering will be further enhanced. PMO
will also continue to produce information material such as how-to videos and visual aids on
how to navigate PMO’s increasingly automated systems.
After having organised online sessions followed by an in-presence day in Brussels in 2025,
feedback on the PMO Training Days will be analysed as to the preference of the participants,
mainly representatives of EUIBA’s who are PMO’s clients. The 2026 edition will be designed
considering the participants’ feedback.
Improved efficiency of IT systems will also facilitate client satisfaction. A specific attention
will be given to the modernisation of existing applications and the optimisation of the MyPMO
mobile application (for the Missions management application MiPS, the Joint Sickness and
Insurance Scheme, the management of experts’ meetings in AGM (Advanced Gateway to
Meetings) and public transport reimbursements in MyCommuting). All improvements and
modifications of applications will continue to be carefully tested with dedicated tester groups
that have been created with the help of our active and post-active beneficiaries.
As regards the modernisation of the Joint Sickness Insurance Scheme (JSIS), efforts will
continue in 2026 on linking up the IT tool for the sickness insurance (ASSMAL) with the Belgian
IT platform (MyCareNet) for the transition to full digital exchange of documents related to
health care. Following the conclusion of the agreement with the Belgian network of “mutuelles”
(MyCareNet), the project has been opened to staff in October 2025 and is now operational for
medical visits with general practitioners and specialists. The scope will be extended to dentists
in Q1 2026 and pharmaceutical products (pharmacies) in 2026. This project, once fully
(1) AIACE - International Association of Former Staff of the European Union
SEPS - Association of Seniors of the European Public Service
6

implemented, will eliminate the need for scanning medical documents and submitting
reimbursement requests for the approximately 80,000 affected beneficiaries, thus optimising
workflows in the coming years.
In September 2025, the PMO and the Luxembourg Hospitals Federation (FHL) signed an
administrative arrangement for simplifying administrative exchanges and the payment of
health care. With the new direct invoicing system, beneficiaries can generate themselves the
certificate of cover to present for admission to the hospital. The PMO receives and pays the
invoices directly from and to the hospital. For the time being, this certificate is available for
hospitalisation, childbirth and heavy outpatient treatment. In 2026, it should be extended to
other outpatient treatments.
Alongside these developments, the PMO is working with DIGIT to replace the current paper-
based hospital invoicing system with a fully digital process. The benefits of “e-invoice” with the
main hospitals in Belgium and Luxembourg (2) include reduced printing (green initiative),
efficiency gains and a lower risk of errors.
Additionally, discussions are still ongoing in view of the signature of an agreement to ensure
access to healthcare in Italy.
Collaborations with other Member States on access to healthcare services are being analysed
together with DG HR alongside the possibility to integrate the JSIS beneficiaries into the
European Exchange of Social Security Information (EESSI).
The PMO concluded a service contract with a third-party administrator to ensure access to the
healthcare providers' network at reduced negotiated rates for staff (and their dependants)
serving in the EU Delegations of USA, Switzerland, Thailand, China and South Africa. The
registration of the target population will be rolled out at the beginning of 2026, including the e-
invoicing of the medical costs (no paper flow either, thus more greening). This initial pilot
should allow PMO to collect a set of credible data on health care costs and prices in specific
countries and enable PMO to decide on next steps for better access to healthcare in other
countries outside or inside the EU.
Following the success of the agreements for Health Screening Programmes in 22 Member
States, negotiations will continue in 2026 with networks of hospitals/health centres in view of
concluding further agreements for health screening and general medical services.
More details on the planned outputs can be found in the performance tables - Annex 1.
(2) Work is ongoing with the Luxembourg authorities (“Fédération des Hôpitaux
Luxembourgeois – FHL”), as part of the agreement concluded in September 2025, to
generalize electronic invoicing.
7

3. Cross-cutting efforts – implementation and
simplification agenda
A wide digital transformation of PMO processes and improved collaboration with clients has
been set up with the implementation of modern, secure and user-centric IT solutions in parallel
with a harmonised reshape of internal processes. Future developments will continue to focus on
increased efficiency, lower cost of control and reduced risk of error.
The PMO will further work on implementing high standards of security and privacy, given the
sensitivity of the data processed while striving for a balance regarding the administrative
burden.
PMO is moving forward with the “One PMO” initiative. The initiative builds on many previous
endeavours to focus on fully aligned and harmonised business processes for the benefit of
clients but also tallies with the HR Transformation project with a single HR Service Desk. The
“One PMO” project will continue in the future, combining the initiatives “Single phone
number”, the virtual merger of the JSIS Front Office, as well as an increased use of the Staff
Centre and of the MyPMO app.
PMO has initiated the revision of the rules on medical reimbursement (General Implementing
Provisions of the JSIS) through internal consultations, establishing dedicated working groups
based on thematic areas and field experience to develop a coherent set of priority changes.
Building on this groundwork, the revision will aim at modernising the JSIS, transforming it from
a static set of rules into a modern sickness insurance system that balances attractiveness with
financial viability. Reimbursement ceilings will be reviewed, and reimbursement processes will
be streamlined, clarified, and made more transparent for beneficiaries.
Agreements with healthcare providers will contribute to enhance predictability and generate
cost savings. The guiding principles of this revision are simplification for both PMO and its
clients. Engagement with other Commission services, CGAM, staff representatives and other EU
Institutions will ensure a successful implementation in a timely manner. Finally, the actual
implementation will have to be phased and aligned with IT readiness.
With the objective to render business processes more efficient and get more value out of large
datasets, PMO is exploring the potential of artificial intelligence in several domains, as laid
down in the PMO AI@EC initiatives in collaboration with the HR Transformation programme.
These initiatives aim at:
• supporting the business process efficiency, especially in areas involving repetitive and
manual tasks, such as checking scanned documents with Intelligent Document
Processing technologies;
• linking information and data, to detect paths or relationships, assess large volumes of
information and identify inconsistent situations, which should allow to improve internal
control through easier error and fraud detection;
• improving the service provided by the colleagues by using virtual assistants and
chatbots, which should benefit from the new generative AI models like GPT@EC;
• enhancing the business analytics and foresight for our management, by introducing AI
components such as deep learning to develop advanced analytics capabilities.
8

To support the PMO’s staff in their efforts to deliver quality services in the context of a
steady increase of transactions, the PMO’s knowledge management (KM) system
encompasses a common knowledge base of procedures and related content, supported by a
powerful Search+ function developed and launched in 2024. The system now features
thematic onboarding packages tailored to each domain and sub-domain, allowing
newcomers to acquire essential knowledge in a structured, centralised manner and become
quickly operational. Taxonomy used to organise and categorise knowledge will be further
developed for domains such as budget, payroll, procurement and travel management. The
existing onboarding packages will be further enriched with legal information and reusable
Q&As.
As regards Document Management, the revision of the PMO filing plan and re-design of
integration of PMO information systems with Hermes-Ares-NomCom (HAN) via the Hermes
Repository Services (HRS) will continue in 2026. Improvement of such integration boosts
process efficiency by automatic registration and filing of records.
9

PART 3. A modern and sustainable public
administration: outputs in 2026
The internal control framework supports sound management and decision-making. In particular,
it ensures that risks to the achievement of objectives are addressed and reduced to acceptable
levels through cost-effective controls.
The Head of Service of PMO has established an internal control system tailored to its
characteristics and circumstances. The effective functioning of this internal control system will
be assessed on an ongoing basis throughout the year and will be subject to an annual
assessment covering all internal control principles.
A. Human resource management
In 2026, the PMO will continue to implement its People Strategy 2030, reinforcing its
commitment to inclusive human resources management and staff well-being. The strategy will
further evolve through a dynamic two-year rolling programme, addressing staff’s feedback and
aligning with the PMO’s management vision. The overarching goal remains to enhance staff
engagement by fostering a supportive, inclusive, and forward-looking work environment. The
PMO People Strategy 2030 is built around three strategic axes:
As part of its strong commitment to career development, the PMO will continue to support staff
in their professional growth. In 2026, the PMO aims to complete two Article 13 screening
exercises with the objective of upgrading around 10% of its current FGII staff to FGIII. This
initiative reflects PMO’s determination to recognise talent, reward performance, and offer
meaningful career progression opportunities. These efforts are complemented by ongoing
initiatives to promote mobility, job shadowing, and targeted training. The action plan
10

underpinning the People Strategy 2030 will be adjusted based on the results of the Staff
Satisfaction Survey launched in October 2025, with results expected over the course of 2026.
These insights will guide the refinement of priorities and ensure alignment with staff
expectations.
In parallel, the PMO will continue to align its recruitment and staffing efforts with operational
priorities, ensuring that the right skills and profiles are available to meet evolving
organisational needs, in full compliance with the Staff Regulations and relevant implementing
rules.
In alignment with the commitment to equality, diversity, and inclusion, the PMO will continue to
maintain gender balance in middle management in 2026. Currently, 57% of Heads of Unit
positions are held by women. By the end of 2026, 61% of pre-management roles will also be
occupied by women. These figures reflect the PMO’s ongoing commitment to fostering gender
equality and preparing women for leadership roles. Information as to results and planned
outputs for 2026 in this area can be found in Annex 2 (page 21).
B. Digital transformation and data management
Digital transformation
PMO continues to drive its digital transformation and is committed to harnessing the power of
technology to enhance its operations and deliver better services to users. PMO’s Senior
Management, Middle Management, and IT Steering Committee are actively involved in steering
local digital transformation initiatives, with key roles played by the Chief Information
Officer/Digital Transformation Officer (Head of Unit PMO.6 Digital Solutions), and Digital
Transformation Coordinators in the PMO.6 Digital Solutions unit. The PMO is also adopting a
local digital strategy, with a common Digital Transformation Initiative at the forefront of its
efforts.
PMO will still be heavily impacted by the Commission’s digital transformation programme in the
financial domain (SUMMA). The third wave of integration of its processes and IT applications
with SUMMA will follow the second wave of 23 EUIBAs migrating from ABAC in January 2026.
This second wave will require full attention beginning of 2026, to support the payment of
salaries and missions, especially with the EEAS and FRONTEX as big consumers of PMO’s
services, while 7 EUIBAs will also use the expert management system, AGM (Advanced Gateway
to Meetings), in full integration with SUMMA.
With the third wave in 2026, PMO will finalise, together with DIGIT and DG BUDG, the work to
integrate the JSIS business and related IT systems with SUMMA, in view of the switch in
January 2027. On top of this integration, additional 27 EUIBAs will move to SUMMA in 2027,
and PMO will need to ensure that the user acceptance testing, the configuration of access
rights and the data migration will be concluded in Q3 2026. This should allow for the switch
from ABAC to SUMMA as of November 2026, with the anticipated 2027 budget.
Strategic Objective 1: Digital Culture
To foster a culture of digital excellence, the PMO will focus on enhancing digital skills through
11

targeted and role-based IT training, promoting EU Learn courses, and involving the PMO HR
Correspondent team in identifying staff training needs. The PMO will also prioritise
cybersecurity awareness, with briefings, training, and awareness campaigns aimed at senior
management, system owners, and all staff. Furthermore, the Office will promote mobile-ready
EC solutions, including its dedicated mobile application, MyPMO, and encourage collaboration
through digital workplace tools like Teams and M365. Finally, a plan will be set up for staff to
acquire AI skills and knowledge, such as training on AI tools and platforms, to support the
successful proposed implementation of AI-driven business processes and innovation.
Strategic Objective 2: Digital-ready policymaking
While the PMO acknowledges the importance of digital-ready policymaking, its current focus is
on building a strong digital foundation to support this objective in its role as supporting service
to the HR family and the central services.
Strategic Objective 3: Business-driven digital transformation
To drive business transformation, the PMO will improve business process modelling and
automation, leveraging AI features and platforms like ServiceNow, SUMMA, Reusable Solutions
Platform, including MyWorkplace/Compass corporate for experts and Open source Peppol. The
Office will also prioritize data openness, maturity, and interoperability, promoting the use of
corporate data services and ensuring interoperability aspects of IT systems. Additionally, the
PMO will foster innovation, mapping our department's needs and capabilities, identifying gaps,
and collaborating on existing initiatives. It will also promote AI training and encourage the use
of Commission-wide AI solutions, implementing existing corporate AI services and empowering
business units to develop new digitally innovative prototypes and systems.
Strategic Objective 4: Seamless digital environment
To achieve a seamless digital environment, the PMO will focus on improving its digital
landscape by replacing, transforming, and migrating IT systems to embed newer technologies
and capabilities. It will also prioritise reusing existing business-agnostic IT solutions, such as
digital sovereign Reusable Solution Platform, and fostering the reusability and interoperability
of its IT systems. The PMO will also ensure an enhanced User Experience for all types of
populations served, especially those more vulnerable population such as pensioners.
Additionally, it will promote cloud adoption whenever possible, conducting an analysis of
current IT systems that could potentially move to the cloud and developing an action plan for
their migration.
Strategic Objective 5: Green, secure and resilient
infrastructure
To ensure a green, secure, and resilient infrastructure, the Office will promote the Digital
Workplace Portal and its informative cards to address staff needs on IT tooling, services, and
skills. The PMO will also recognize and balance the need to reduce risk and enhance maturity in
cybersecurity, ensuring that all necessary controls are put in place and monitored.
In addition, further improvement can be obtained by taking into consideration the
implementation of actions outlined in the EC Cybersecurity Strategy for 2025-2026, as
designated in the Commission’s Cybersecurity Plan 2025-2026 and the strengthening of the IT
12

sovereignty and resilience by 1) ensuring mapping of third-party dependencies and the
supply chain and gaining/maintaining control of critical assets, data, and operations; and 2) by
implementing robust measures to prevent, detect, and respond to disruptions or threats, in full
compliance with applicable EU laws and regulations and in line with the European Commission's
IT security and resilience standards.
Furthermore, it will locally promote IT greening, pursuing actions such as applying the 'less
paper' policy but leaving some openness to vulnerable populations such as pensioners,
promoting energy-efficient data exchanges, and eliminating paper and scanned documents
wherever possible. Following the migration to the Welcome domain of all PMO devices, a
continuous monitoring and auditing of the access rights under the supervision of the internal
control team will continue in 2026.
Data management
Data is a crucial asset for the PMO and plays a fundamental role in the execution of its
mandate. In previous years the PMO has undertaken significant efforts to improve its data
maturity posture, achieving a 'Developing' data maturity level in the four areas of interest
related to data: Data Management, Data ownership and responsibilities, Data Quality &
FAIRness and Data Skills.
Data Management, Data ownership and responsibilities: The PMO works in close cooperation
with the other members of the HR Family in the domain of Data Management, notably in the
context of the HRT Digital Transformation programme. Steps towards a closer integration and
alignment are foreseen in the upcoming waves of the programme, including common Data
Governance practices, a common Data Catalogue and a common Data Platform which is
currently in the initial design phase.
Given the key financial impact for PMO, with the arrival of SUMMA, more synergies with DG
BUDG will be sought in the data governance area. This will allow to have a crosscutting and
end-to-end overview of all financial data impacting PMO’s business.
Data Quality & FAIRness: In addition to the actions already foreseen in the context of the HRT
programme a key initiative in this area will be the creation of data quality dashboards providing
a horizontal view across IT systems. These will provide business units with a user-centric view
of key data assets and provide actionable metrics on Data Quality and FAIRness.
Data Skills: PMO will continue to promote the upskilling of staff through both external and
internal trainings, also in the context of the use of Artificial Intelligence. Hands-on trainings on
the use of available data products (e.g. domain-specific dashboards) will continue to be
organised through the year. This will also allow to identify new data needs and plan future
data-related developments.
Because of the particular nature of the mandate of the PMO, for the moment no relevant data
assets to be published at the data.europa.eu portal have been identified.
13

As the HRT Programme will move forward in the coming years and as the members of the HR
Family develop and align their data governance practices, the PMO expects to reach the level
'Established' in all four areas.
Data protection
Regarding data protection, the PMO will continue to implement the action plan in response to
the IAS audit report on PMO's personal data protection, adopted in 2024.
As regards the accountability principle, PMO has already established procedures to clearly
outline the roles and responsibilities of controllers, clearly set out the organisational structure
for managing data protection and will continue ensuring that operational roles in place support
the practical implementation of data protection.
The PMO continues to fulfil its obligations as separate controller when processing personal data
in the context of the Service Level Agreements concluded with Union institutions, agencies and
other bodies, as well as in the context of agreements with parties established in the Union
other than Union institutions and bodies. Regarding data exchanges between the PMO and the
Member States, the PMO will carefully assess the potential impact of the envisaged data
processing operations on data subjects and conduct a Data Protection Impact Assessment,
where the conditions set out in Article 39 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 are met. Furthermore,
the PMO will continue to include a data protection annex in all agreements concluded, to
reinforce transparency towards data subjects and clearly define the roles and responsibilities of
the parties involved.
Records and privacy statements will continue to be reviewed in accordance with the DPO’s
guidelines, and the dedicated webpage on the PMO Intranet will be regularly updated to make
them accessible to data subjects.
In 2026, the PMO will continue to conduct regular training sessions aimed at raising and
sustaining staff awareness on the importance of protecting personal data and cybersecurity.
General trainings on Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 will be provided to staff members across all
PMO units complemented by specialized training sessions addressing key topics of relevance
(i.e. data breaches, handling data subject requests, records of processing operation etc.). These
trainings are regularly updated to consider the latest developments in the field and integrate
the lessons learned.
Concerning the data protection by design and by default obligation, the data protection
coordinator of the PMO participates in the IT decision-making meetings to ensure that data
protection is embedded in the design of information systems and processes.
The PMO continues its internal reflection, in collaboration with other services of the
Commission, to find alternative solutions for projects that involve cloud technology or
international transfers. These efforts aim to ensure that such transfers are carried out lawfully
are and in full compliant with Chapter V of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 and the relevant case
law.
14

The PMO will continue its collaboration with the DPOs of other EUIs or other DPCs of other
services of the Commission via meetings on specific topics. Information as to results and
planned outputs for 2026 in the area can be found in Annex 2 (page 22).
C. Sound financial management
The PMO’s control strategy presents the methodology and procedure of controls carried out in
the PMO. The control objective is to contribute to management assurance regarding legality and
regularity of operations, taking into account the three building blocks (effectiveness, efficiency
and economy) of sound financial management. The PMO has set up internal control processes
aimed at ensuring the adequate management of identified risk.
Since the business of the PMO is characterised by high numbers of transactions, many of which
are processed through mass operations, important developments have taken place in areas of
secure and user-centric IT solutions in parallel with a general reshaping of internal processes.
These developments are expected to have a positive impact on the level of risk as well as the
overall cost of controls.
The objective is to maintain the risk at payment below the materiality threshold of 2%,
confirming the accuracy and quality of transactions processed by the PMO and the
effectiveness of the ex-ante controls. Information as to results and planned outputs for 2026 in
this area can be found in Annex 2 (page 24).
D. Fraud risk management
The PMO has developed and implemented its own anti-fraud strategy since 2013, based on the
methodology provided by OLAF. It is updated every 3 years, last time in 2022. The Anti-Fraud
Strategy is currently under revision, the updated version to be adopted in 2026. The PMO
contributes to the Commission’s anti-fraud strategy (revised CAFS action plan 2023) in the
action towards awareness raising, while it also actively participates in the Commission’s Fraud
Prevention and Detection Network and its subgroups.
The new PMO anti-fraud strategy will be structured around three major objectives:
• Improve communication: Following a successful campaign in 2025, a new anti-fraud
awareness-raising training in collaboration with OLAF will be planned for 2026.
• Increase the use of IT tools and digital exchange of data for fraud detection: To
carry out its tasks, the PMO uses several IT applications that generate large amounts of
usable data. Data analysis allows for detecting discrepancies and selecting cases where
the risk of fraud is greatest for targeted and cost-effective controls.
• Ensure feedback of fraud cases to improve processes and control: The regular ex-
post controls, as well as specific anti-fraud related checks are embedded in the internal
control strategy. The PMO Internal Control sector ascertains the appropriate treatment
of all potential cases (transfer to OLAF and IDOC).
15

The strategy’s implementation is being monitored and reported to the management, as part of
the state of play on internal control. The authorising officers by sub-delegation (AOSD) report
on their activities to the Head of Service with the obligation to explicitly mention any anomalies
that occurred. Information as to results and planned outputs for 2026 in this area can be found
in Annex 2 (page 24).
E. Sound environmental management
The Corporate EU Eco-Management and Audit Scheme (EMAS) policy is implemented by the
PMO. Next to the initiatives managed at central level, local actions in the PMO sites are set up
for promoting an environmental-friendly working place and making better use of natural
resources, in line with the Communication of the Greening the Commission whereby the
Commission’s ambition is to become climate neutral by 2030.
The current set-up of PMO’s buildings as a collaborative space facilitates sustainable ways of
working and energy efficiency. Teleworking, coupled with growing use of paperless processes,
collaborative tools and video conferencing, reduces PMO’s environmental footprint.
Taking advantage of existing capabilities in the applications and platforms used, the PMO uses
paperless workflows for the majority of its procedures. Declarations and exchange of
information with PMO’s clients are mainly processed through online tools.
Under the umbrella of the Digital Communication Programme, in 2026 the PMO will continue to
map and analyse remaining paper circuits and possibilities for digitalisation in order to further
reduce paper consumption and improve “paperless” exchanges with DG HR – to the extent
possible, given the vulnerable populations it also serves.
In the area of healthcare, ongoing efforts to extend digital invoicing by healthcare practitioners
and hospitals in several Member States will contribute to decrease the environmental footprint,
by reducing the paperwork and simplifying the workflows.
PMO contributes towards raising awareness on the ecological impact of missions by measuring
the impact of each mission and suggest options to limit the impact to various actors. The
baseline (in 2019) for the staff travel emissions in PMO is 48.119,07 Kg CO2. The aim is to
reduce by 50% until 2030, in line with the corporate target. For 2026, developments in the
EULP procedures will contribute to this objective. PMO is following up on the developments in
the field of Green public procurement and adapting its procedures to the new features where
applicable.
The EMAS campaigns envisaged in 2026 will continue to focus on staff awareness on greener
ways of working, waste reduction and energy saving. Local actions will be supported by regular
publication of tips and tricks on the dedicated PMO EMAS Intranet page. PMO will also
encourage its staff to become EU Climate Pact ambassadors. Information as to results and
planned outputs for 2026 in this area can be found in Annex 2. (page 25).
16
